>Who else made the finals?
I couldn´t see all decks clearly, so for some I am not that sure what they
actually played, but here´s my best guess.
The Ruben who won the German Qualifier (no VP), Martin from Austria
(Malks)(no VP), a guy I didn´t know (Arika)(no VP) and the always infamous
BEN PEAL (Malkav bleed)(2VP), who grapped the vice European Champion Title.
At the start of the game there was a lot of talk of Ruben convinving the
spanish Ruben to attack Martin, who had a lot of intercept. To help the War
Ghouls Ruben called a Dramatic Upheaval to get the Warghouls as his prey,
Ben Peal as his grand prey, Martin as his Grand Predator and the Arika Deck
as his predator.
The War Ghouls attacked Martin, Ben bled a lot and so eventually Martin was
gone. After that the War Ghouls went for Rubens predator as he diablerized a
high cap vampire of Ruben and so posed a high threat to him. That left him
no options and Ben Peal bled the hell out of him. Until that time the War
Ghouls had a peace treaty with their predator (Ruben). Well, as I said,
until then: Ben playing with a lot of small caps left all the minion who
were gone to torpor in their state the whole game, so a few rushes disposed
him of ready vampires and a dragon bound ousted him. Shortly after that
Ruben was ousted.
So we have a worthy european European Champion!
Again Congrats to Ruben Vidaña (sorry for using your name so scarcely for
making clearer who is who)

had tapped out with no Wakes and 5-6 intercept cards in hand. I was
able to bleed for 7 one last time with Gratiano, and that was all that
was necesssary to take Erik.)

Messages.Author: Daneel
Messages.Body:
On 27 Nov 2004 13:03:13 -0800, Joshua Duffin <jtdu...@yahoo.com> wrote:

> Isn't anyone going to weblog the European Championships? We need
> on-the-ground reporting! :-)

Saturday I was playing Knights, a Ventrue Antitribu AUS FOR deck.

Table 1:

Temptation + Vampiric Disease deck
Jay Kristoff with Nosferatu Antitribu
Potence Dominate Rush Bleed
Synesios and co. pre obf vote and misc
Daneel's Knights

Jay controlled the table from round 1. He was a very verbal player (not
my preference), and the table eventually reached the point when he was
the strongest. I had a bad initial draw, with 6 combat cards and no way
to really use them. My prey - thanks to an odd deck concept or Jay's
mood control - Tempted each and every vampire on the table *except* for
any of Jay's guys. I'm not sure what the master plan was, but it sure
didn't work. So I took risks in the hopes of getting at least 1 VP and
dropped Dragonbound. My prey then struck a deal with Jay, who offered
him 1 VP if he clears the way. He took everyone (except for the
PotDom's newly influenced Isabel and my newly influenced Juan Cali)
and diablerized his own minions and the minions cross-table. I blocked
my Dominique but every other minion got burned. Then Isabel rushed
Kephamos, my prey's last minion, and tore his hands off. I bled but I
didn't draw any bleed, so Jay ousted two in a sequence. My next turn
promised to be the last, and I had my chance as my prey was at 2 and I
had 2 minions and Dominique had a Melange in effect. I bled with her in
a damned if you block (Dragonbound) and damned if you don't way - except
for the fact that Kephamos was playing dominate bounce... ;) After my
oust the game ended in a Discard-fest that is so very beautiful about
VTES. Ah well, at least Jay kept his word.

Table 2:

Arika & co. Stealth Vote
TheLasombra with Lasombra combat
Helena gun block Smiling Jack
Zsolt Toth with Gargoyles
Daneel's Knights

Arika PTOed TheLasombra's Banjoko, who rewarded my prey with
Fame and Haven. I however did not have a hand even remotely
adequate to beat a full 11-cap, so I reluctantly passed the
opportunity. I was bleeding some but then my prey gained pool
like hell. My predator drew no Tremere in his opening crypt,
so I had a few free turns, but this was not sufficient to
ofset my erratic draw. I also knew Zsolt's deck, because I
already sat next to it (or its predecessor) during casual
games before the EC and each and every time we ended up
beating the crap out of eachother. We both knew that once
he gets rolling things will get grim for the both of us, so
I hoped to oust before that and withstand him by going only
forward. The plan fizzled as I was unable to oust my prey,
but then Helena got her gun and proved to be a major pain in
the ass for the Gargoyles. My prey switched places with the
Helena deck and eventually got ousted by TheLasombra just
before time. I'm not sure if Jeff is a genius or got lucky,
but putting a Fame on Arika ten rounds before she becomes
his prey is smooth beyond comprehension. ;) 1,5 to
TheLasombra and 0,5 to all but the Arika deck.

Table 3:

Theo Bell and friends POT rush deck
Lasombra fatty vote
Martin Major with dom obf stealth bleed
Eurobrujah
Daneel's Knights

I had the least bad draw on the day. I might've won this
game if it only lasted two or three more hours. ;P As that
was not the case, we ended up in a more or less static
stalemate. Martin got ousted by the table wrath but everyone
else stayed to time. 1,5 for the Lasombra deck and 0,5 for
everyone else.

Sunday I was playing an old school Ventrue Law Firm.

Table 1:

Oko (Tariq)
Gangrel "I have 40 copies of Earth Meld" wall
Gábor Balázs with Auspex Celerity and Magnums
Simona Siracusa with Toreador - !Toreador Stealth Bleed
Daneel's Law Firm

Now, if I hadn't been the one to advise Gábor, the Prince
of Budapest to play his Celerity Guns deck just the day
before, because he plays it well, I wouldn't have felt so
silly. Or, if the tables hadn't been rearranged in the
last minute because of some late arrivals or drops
(placing me at Gábor's table). I did not really want to
face him, as my combat defences were abysmal, but I still
wasn't really worried as Simona was sitting between us.
My prey was unlucky, as Gábor used all his sidekicks, so
he was left with Zöe and Tariq (while his prey had
Aranthebes). I ousted him but then Gábor ousted Simona
and myself, and was left in a lockdown with the other
wall. They fought for about an hour and then the
Gangrel's library got depleted, and they agreed that
since it was less than a minute to time, he would
withdraw. 3 for Gábor, 1 for me and the Gangrel.

Table 2:

FOR DOM THA unpreventable prerange aggravated deck
Eric Chiang with POT CEL combat
EuroBrujah Rush
Tibor Holhos with dominate weenies that bleed for 3 at 1 stealth
Daneel's Law Firm

I was very unSunTzuesque in appearing strong when in
reality I was not. I knew I'll get fucked but I had
no options to be subtle. I called one Parity Shift
on my prey, who then stopped playing and said "I'm
not going to help you oust my prey." Great VTES
philosophy, especially since I had support cards in
my hand but no votes or bleed. I needed to influence
out more guys to get more pool via Boons and Voter,
but being bled for 6 or so each turn placed a pressure
on me that I wasn't equipped to handle from my current
hand. I knew that my predator plays a very straight-
forward VTES, which I greatly admire, but which is a
terrible philosophy for one's predator. So I knew that
I will be hammered heavily from round 1 and I was
quite right. I was ultimately ousted after Eric rushed
my only untapped vampire cross-table. He then
proceeded to win the game, with my original prey
slipping to my original predator as well. 2 for Tibor
and 3 for Eric. The moral of the story is, they no
longer play this game for VPs but GWs. Eric knew he
had more combat than his prey or Tibor, but feared
that if I lunged (which I really hoped to do) I might
oust him quickly.

Table 3:

Francois Morand with Anson Anthelios Master
Old School Nosferatu Bruise and Vote
Zsolt Cziráki with Nosferatu Antitribu wall
Dimitrios Kotsis with DEM OBF stealth bleed
Daneel's Law Firm

This round gets more attention as there is a deal break involved.
Dimitrios started strong and I got bled for quite a
lot. I was also extremely far from having vote lock,
controlling about a quarter of all the votes at the
table. My priority became gaining pool, and I had to
make a coupla short term non-aggression packs with
my prey. I was preparing my ousting hand in the
meantime, knowing that I'm not any better off if
Dimitrios gets ousted, because Zsolt will block my
actions (no stealth) and I'll be minionless in no
time (the only thing worse than being short on pool).
So by the time I got back to playing the game after
my predator was sufficiently pummeled, I was facing
a prey with about 15 pool and three MPAs with
Anthelios in play. I started going forward, and
Zsolt ousted Dimitrios - who got saved by my prey's
Life Boon. My prey seemed pretty strong nevertheless,
and I was about at 6 pool with two princes and
nothing more. So next round I told my predator that
if he ousted my prey, I would make sure he gets at
least 1 VP by transfering out if the time limit
approached. This way I wold get at least 1 VP myself.
We were approaching time, and Dimitrios knew that
the Life Boon would steel his VP.

The game state at this point was something like:

Me: 6 pool, Timothy Crowley and Wilhelm Waldburg, Ventrue HQ
Francois Morand: 15 pool, Anson, Democritus, Anthelios, Parthenon
Other French guy (sorry, I forgot): 5 pool, Sheldon and Nikolaus
Zsolt: 1 pool, Teresita and Ox, Hunting Ground
Dimitrios: 5 pool, Rodolfo out, Dolphin Black and Quentin King III in
torpor

So Dimitrios bled Francois for 2×3 and passed the
turn. I called Parity Shift with Waldburg which my
prey DI-ed. I then called Conservative Agitation
with Timothy, doing 4 damage to my prey and 1
damage to myself, pushed the vote and passed it. I
then bled with Waldburg. My prey asked me: "Why do
you bleed me?" Well, 'cause you're my prey. I played
Daring the Dawn and Conditioning, and the latter got
DIed by the other french guy, when Francois promised
him not to play Anarch Revolt or bleed during his
turn. I passed the turn. Francois played Anarch
Revolt and bled with both vampires, so the AR killed
his prey (and then Zsolt) when he passed the turn.
When Dimitrios started his turn, Francois told him
that he should oust me (giving him the VP) and then
he'll allow him to withdraw... As if he hadn't
broken his promise not one minute ago. The game
timed out during my turn and the results were
Francois 3 VP (2,5 + 0,5 from Dimitrios) and me 0,5 VP.

It was sad how Francois broke his word even though he
had no chance of making the finals. He won but he
needed to make a deal explicitly in order to break it
(as the 1 pool his prey spent on the DI was what
allowed him to attempt the oust in the first place).
I'm also not sure what the other French guy expected,
but he was playing well the whole game so I'm sure
there was no collusion involved (he was shocked when
Francois broke his word). By the way Francois seemed
like a nice guy and it was fun playing with him.
However, the bottom line is that he has proven capable
of breaking a deal in our game.

All in all it was a fun EC and the organizers did a
good job. I had more fun than VPs though... ;) I hope
to see more interesting ECs.

--
Bye,

Daneel

case when bluffing is permitted). I'm using "honest" in the
former sense -- refusal to break / adherence to the rules/law.

much better than your opponents (as in V:TES), most games are not
against inferior opponent and you will be forced to deal well for
position (as in V:TES) and possibly even break those deals (as in

You're right. Players are assumed to try to win in the methods allowed
by the rules - I never assume a player is trying to cheat by breaking
the rules, for an 'all costs' example.

However, given that there have been specific statements _from the
people who oversee the game as a whole_ about when you are and are not
required to honor a deal, and that there are common circumstances
which deal-breaking is definitely allowed, I (and most rational
people) would assume that the possibility of someone breaking a deal
is therefore an accepted part of the game and not unthinkably
dishonest like cheating.

With regards to lying (as opposed to cheating):

Consider the Monocle of Clarity: if the average player was assumed to
be honest about something like whether or not they currently have a
2nd tradition in their hand, a card that forces that honesty as a game
mechanic would never have been created in the first place - and if
insuring that honesty were universally important to the creators of
the game, that mechanic would have been stated universally instead of
only conditionally on a piece of equipment.

Consider that the tournament rules (i.e. stricter than casual play)
PROHIBIT you from proving to another player that your statement about
the content of your hand is true or not - you are not allowed to show
hidden information (like a card in your hand) to other players unless
they have a mechanic that allows them to make you do so.

Consider that the game developer has directly stated 'yes you can lie'
about a variety of topics, even as to whether or not a player has lied
in the past!

Consider that there ARE things that you are specifically not allowed
to lie about - such as the relative capacity of the target of a
Govern, even though in a tournament you cannot show the other players
the card, only a judge. Note that the rules are thus 'you cannot lie
about things X, Y, Z' not 'you cannot lie',

So, given that there are some things that the game prohibits you from
lying about, and there are other things that the game _specifically
permits_ you to lie about, why would you assume that lying about those
permitted things is an 'at all costs' method of winning to be avoided
and chastised, as opposed to a widely accepted, deliberately included
part of the game and its strategy?

you have a 2nd' is so bad, why not just insist on everybody playing
the game with every card face-up? Cause if you are going to be
scrupulously honest at all times, I'll gladly, continually ask
questions about everything I want to know about your deck, your hand,
and your game, secure in the knowledge that you'd never, ever 'stoop'
to lying or being less than completely honest to me in response, and
there won't be any need for any game information to ever be hidden.
:P)
